sourceInformation.source: Pitfall! (1982), designed by David Crane and published by Activision
sourceInformation.perspective: 2.5D side view with a scrolling orthographic camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 WebGPURenderer (WebGPU, automatic WebGL 2 fallback); Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded jungle dioramas with ink contours, engraved ruins and a warm paper palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for explorer poses, crocodile jaws, cobras, scorpions and treasures; procedural pendulum vines, particles and foliage
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated pentatonic marimba music at 10% by default, synthesized effects, filtered Animalese-style gibberish and procedural percussion; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1 ghost races for 1–4 players; standalone shared-screen co-op for two players
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 / Playwright 1.63.0 with software WebGPU, normal-control complete expedition, keyboard and emulated standard gamepads, landscape/portrait touch, file:// sharing, save/load, defeat/victory, attract replay, live analyser and offline synthesized audio. AI Hub harness: 2 players, 4 players at 150 ms latency / 50 ms jitter / 5% packet loss, and host departure. WebGL 2 screenshots for visual review. Physical controller, real touch device, hardware GPU rendering and audio listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original Activision Pitfall! manual: 255 circular scenes, 32 treasures, three lives, 20-minute clock, surface hazards and faster underground route. David Crane retrospective interview for vine and crocodile inspiration; VGMPF for the original sparse sound palette. Original level, characters, art and score in this demo.

testingFeedback: 8 product issues across API checks, automated tests and visual/control review; all resolved. Test-driver mistakes are excluded.
3 would have blocked loading or normal movement: the Rapier import path, descriptor methods and inactive second-player collision.

The complete expedition driven by normal movement, jump and climb controls without cheats or teleporting: eight treasures, four vine swings, both caves and the victory screen. The AI Hub harness also verified all three applicable network scenarios.
Headless software WebGPU screenshots were blank. State checks verified WebGPU execution, and WebGL 2 captures were useful for visual review instead.
engineFeedback: Three.js native animation clips and toon materials work together through WebGPURenderer, and Rapier provides reliable collision queries and a capsule controller.
I initially used an incorrect Rapier module filename and confused rigid-body descriptor methods with runtime rigid-body methods. Checking the pinned 0.19.3 package corrected both before release.
The platform controller and vine handoff rules, controller-first menus, expedition/save state, procedural jungle, code-only audio and ghost presentation.
Coordinating native animation blending with collision-safe jumps, moving jaws and pendulum vines, while keeping the side-view route readable.
A maintained end-to-end WebGPU toon/outline example with a native animated character controller and deterministic headless validation.
promptFeedback: The specific source, art direction, controller-first requirements, attract mode and single-file package gave the demo a clear identity and a concrete definition of done.
The preferred multiplayer mode and whether standalone play required an internet transport were unspecified. I chose shared-screen co-op outside the hub and online ghost races inside it.
Keeping gameplay, menus, audio and lifecycle consistent across keyboard, standard controllers, touch and multiplayer sessions.
Specify the desired multiplayer relationship and whether standalone internet matchmaking or direct connections are required.

aiHub.name: Pitfalling for Adventure
aiHub.tagline: Mind the gap. And the teeth.
aiHub.description: Swing through an ink-drawn jungle, brave snapping crocodiles and explore the tunnels below to recover eight lost treasures. Play alone, share the trail in local co-op, or race ghost explorers in AI Hub.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / A,D; jump and release vine: Cross / Space; climb: up,down / W,S; map: Triangle / M; pause: Options / Esc. Local P2: arrows + Right Shift, or a second pad. Touch: left drag, right tap.
